role: Exact all-12 higher-order joint-charge discriminator and complete-second-law closure on one selected first public record
question: Do any three-, four- or five-site second-charge correlations distinguish one of the twelve same-first-record private errors from the base under the fixed loop action, after all single and pair moments matched?
source_basis: J7Y fixes all zero one-/two-site selected-first moments across all twelve errors and both actions
J7M fixes both exact base complete second public laws
J7V fixes exact complete second laws of the two five-edge peers as independent controls
J7T fixes all twelve positive-mass same-first private errors and first masses
frozen_model: Same paper-normalized ideal periodic L=2 D4 orbit, pre-existing 36-red-edge physical red-X errors, one selected complete first binary public record, and relation-free actions [0] or [1,30,32,34,35]. The error remains private; neither action observes it. No new support, geometry, rate, noisy instrument, score or policy.

matrix.design: For base and every twelve candidates, compute all ten order-three, five order-four and one order-five second-star parity moments under the loop action; no higher-order moment exists for the single-site action. Combine these with J7Y's pinned one-/two-site moments and the deterministic 21/17 other eligible charges, then invert the full Walsh transform over one or five bits. This covers both fixed public actions for all thirteen private errors, not only a preferred peer.
matrix.method: Reuse J7Y's exact selected-first projector/orbit-moment identity and anticommutation shortcut. For each bit string x of k variable sites, P(x)=2^-k sum_{S subset sites} (-1)^(sum_{i in S}x_i) M(S), with M(empty)=1 and all nonempty M from pinned J7Y or this new high-order calculation. Insert the frozen complete second flux and public charge/vacuum arrays. A moment difference proves a complete-law difference; a full Walsh reconstruction with all 2^k rows closes equality or difference exactly.
matrix.integrity: Pins before and after; same error list, exact first masses and first/second public flux; commuting first/second operator sets; all 208 high-order moments present; exact nonnegative rational probabilities and unit normalization; reconstructed base laws exactly equal J7M and two peer laws exactly equal J7V under both actions. Fail closed on any mismatch.
matrix.uncertainty: Finite exact rational selected-record laws, so no sampling interval; selection and ideal L=2 orbit limit interpretation. This matrix does not evaluate a full-IID prior, logical loss or a noisy JIT policy.

acceptance: All twelve candidate-by-two-action cells plus two base controls and their registered 208 high-order moments are complete
All positive complete public rows are exact rational, nonnegative, unique and normalized; base and both peer controls replay prior exact full laws
Report equality or difference only for the thirteen-error support, selected first record, two actions and ideal L=2 orbit; no full-IID or logical-risk generalization
No new histories, arms, bootstrap, ordered projector expansion or threshold work

outcomes.some_different_complete_law: Retain every positive candidate/action witness and preregister a bounded restricted-support information analysis before any logical-risk or noisy-policy inference.
outcomes.all_equal_complete_law: The second public record cannot distinguish these thirteen private errors under either action on this selected first-record slice; seek a separately registered error/first-record/geometry discriminator, not a full-IID null.
outcomes.censored: On any pin, mass, flux, algebra, Walsh, positivity, replay, cap or runtime failure, release no complete-law conclusion.

stop_rule: Stop after 208 high-order moments and 26 fixed complete-law cells or sooner on a gate failure. No new physical errors, full-IID posterior, logical risk, stochastic history or JIT policy evaluation.
